{{Quote|I am Lord Clados Vader. I have your friend.|Clados Vader to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="SW87" />}}
'''Clados Vader''' was a mysterious [[Changeling/Legends|changeling]] entity who dwelled in the oceans of [[Iskalon/Legends|Iskalon]]. It was a giant deformed [[Shark/Legends|shark]], and it could turn into the shape of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], Clados was killed by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] for having captured the [[Gold/Legends|golden]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|It's C-3PO. I'm being held on Iskalon. Come save me!|C-3PO calling Luke Skywalker for help|<ref name="SW87" />}}
Clados Vader was a malevolent [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifter]] who lived on the [[Water/Legends|oceanic]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Iskalon/Legends|Iskalon]],<ref name="SW87" /> in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] Territories.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> It could assume the appearance of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]&mdash;hence the creature's name.<ref name="SW87" />

Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destruction]] of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]], Clados Vader took the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] hostage in an underwater chamber. [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] came to rescue his friend and confronted the monster, who had metamorphosed into Lord Vader. One swipe of the [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi apprentice's]] [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and the fake Vader transformed back into its real form, an enormous [[Shark/Legends|shark]]-like creature with a pinkish [[Color/Legends|hue]]. After the shapeshifter was defeated, Luke Skywalker and C-3PO set off to battle the Death Star.<ref name="SW87" />

==Behind the scenes==
Clados Vader was one of the stage bosses in the Japanese [[Star Wars (1987 video game)|''Star Wars'' 1987 video game]].<ref name="SW87" /> The game featured various fake Vaders which all happened to be shapeshifting monsters. The canonicity of this game and the creatures it features is dubious.

According to both "[[Game On!]]," an article published in [[Star Wars Insider 135|''Star Wars Insider'' 135]], and the game manual, the fake Vaders (Clados, [[Gyaos Vader|Gyaos]], [[Sasori Vader|Sasori]] and [[Wampa Vader|Wampa]]) were "intended as illusions representing Luke's fears, like the [[Cave of Evil/Legends|Cave of Evil]] scene in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Empire Strikes Back'']]."<ref name="SWI135">{{InsiderCite|135|Game On!}}</ref> However, since those game opponents were able to kidnap Luke Skywalker's allies and hold them prisoner,<ref name="SW87" /> this article assumes they were real creatures rather than illusions. Additionally, the Vader-shaped figure that Skywalker fought in the Cave of Evil was more than mere illusion, being in fact a protean [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] entity known as the [[Dark Spirit]].<ref name="toy">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Power of the Jedi|pack=Darth Vader (Dagobah)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/potjdagvader.asp}}</ref>

In the original [[Wikipedia:Japanese language|Japanese]] version, he was identified via [[Wikipedia:Katakana|katakana]] syllabary as クラドスベーダー (''Kuradosu Beidā''). While ''Beidā'' is a transliteration of "Vader" in Japanese, the element クラドス (''kuradosu'') derives from the Japanese name of shark genera, as examplified by the zoological names クラドセラケ (''Cladoselache'') and クラドダス (''Cladodus'').
